title: Graduated Return After Military Service: Age of the Loan
content:
**Rule.** For a Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit of the Hardship Assistance Programs, a loan funded at least 36 whole calendar months before the end of military service adds 2 graduated-return due dates; one funded at least 24 but fewer than 36 months before it adds 1; a younger loan, or a benefit with no captured end of military service, adds none, a month counting as complete only when the later date reaches the funding day of the month. The funding date is the one on the loan's Personal Loans record.

## Questions the rule answers

**From which date to which date are the months counted?** From the loan's funding date to the end of military service captured on the benefit.

**What are the bands?** 36 whole months or more: 2. 24 to 35 whole months: 1. Fewer than 24, or no end of service captured: none.

**When is a month complete?** Only when the later date reaches the funding day of the month. A loan funded on 18 April (hypothetical) has 35 whole months on 17 April three years later and 36 on 18 April three years later.

**A hypothetical case:** funded 5 January, end of military service 4 January two years later: 23 whole months, none; on 5 January two years later it would be 24, adding 1.
